department: Paul H. O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs

deadline.value: Apply by January 1; applications open September 1.
deadline.quote: Applications open September 1 Deadline to apply for all applicants: January 1 Note: Admission decisions for fall admission are typically made by the program by early March

supervisor.value: Students are not admitted unless a faculty member matches their research; contacting advisors beforehand is highly recommended.
supervisor.quote: students are not admitted unless there is a match with a faculty.

funding.value: Admitted students usually get a tuition waiver, health insurance and a stipend ($30,000 for 2026-27).
funding.quote: Students admitted to the O’Neill School Environmental Science Ph.D. program usually receive a 100% tuition and fee waiver, university-paid health insurance, and a stipend

entry_route.value: A bachelor's in science, math or engineering is enough; a master's is not required.
entry_route.quote: A Master’s degree is not required for admission.

gre_general.value: Not stated on the pages checked

toefl_min.value: Not stated on the pages checked

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

notes: Ph.D. in Environmental Science; applies through the University Graduate School. GRE is not on the program's document list.
